vars.prTitle: LoginFailuresUpdater: record changes instead of mutating the read entity
vars.prBody: LoginFailuresUpdater applied every change both to the entity it read from the remote cache and, on commit, to the cached entity in apply(). Keep the read entity untouched and only record the changes; apply() already replays them on commit. Renamed addAndApplyChange to recordChange to reflect that.
vars.goldenComments: [{"comment": "LoginFailuresUpdater (the remote-cache UserLoginFailureModel implementation) no longer applies changes to getValue(). Two pieces of code outside the diff depend on getValue() being up to date: (1) RemoteChangeLogTransaction commits created entries with putIfAbsentAsync(key, updater.getValue(), ...) and read entries with replaceWithVersionAsync(key, updater.getValue(), version, ...) (lines 243/248); apply() is only used on the compute fallback. So a new login-failure record is stored with zero failures and an updated one is replaced with its unchanged value: increments, lockouts and notBefore are silently lost. (2) DefaultBruteForceProtector.failure() calls incrementFailures() and immediately reads getNumFailures()/getNumTemporaryLockouts() to compute waitSeconds and permanent lockout, which the embedded implementation (UserLoginFailureAdapter via InfinispanChangelogBasedTransaction.addTask, which runs the update immediately 'so reader in same transaction can see it') guarantees. Net effect: with the remote/multi-site login-failure provider, brute-force protection never locks users out.", "severity": "High"}]
